title: Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán meets Vladimir Putin in Moscow
body:
On Friday 5 July 2024, Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán visited Moscow and met Russian President Vladimir Putin. It was a rare visit by a European leader since the full-scale invasion; the only other European leader to visit Moscow in that period was Austrian Chancellor Karl Nehammer in April 2022. The trip came days after Orbán had visited Kyiv, where he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and proposed an immediate ceasefire. Hungary had taken over the six-month rotating presidency of the Council of the EU at the beginning of July.

Orbán's press chief, Bertalan Havasi, called the trip a "peace mission". Putin said he was ready to discuss the "nuances" of peace proposals and wanted to hear Orbán's view on Ukraine and what other European partners thought. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Ukraine was on the agenda.

EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell said the visit took place "exclusively, in the framework of the bilateral relations between Hungary and Russia", and that Orbán had no mandate from the EU Council. He added that the EU's position "excludes official contacts between the E.U. and President Putin." Orbán was widely seen as Putin's closest partner in the EU and had often blocked, delayed or diluted EU efforts to aid Ukraine or sanction Russia. He has long called for a halt to hostilities without saying what it would mean for Ukraine's territory or security.
